title: PROVING GROUND: SURFACE AND BRAKING
subtitle: A repeatable engineering course for dry, gravel, mud, ice, ramps, and cross-slope tests.
briefing: This is a measurement course, not a scripted success route.
Surface material, contact, slip, and braking are simulated by the plant.
Use Engineering view for physics evidence and Sandbox H for manual control.

prediction.question: What should a robot do when a surface reduces measured traction?

choices.label: Slow down and preserve stopping distance
choices.explanation: The robot should react to measured motion evidence while keeping its safety footprint fixed.

choices.label: Read the simulator friction value
choices.explanation: Material truth belongs to SIM and is never a ROBOT input.

choices.label: Keep demanding speed until it moves
choices.explanation: A larger command cannot make an unsafe contact envelope safe.

running_prompt: Drive the course manually or let the route run. Compare contact, slip, and braking evidence with the ROBOT decision.

lessons: A continuous surface is part of the physical plant, not a render-only height offset.
Manual driving still passes through the same validator, raw-scan Safety gate, and watchdog.
A failed test is useful evidence when the physical limit is real and reproducible.
